channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Environmental – Wastewater treatment facility – G.L.c. 214, § 7A
item.description: Where a plaintiff seeking to curb nitrogen discharge from a wastewater treatment facility owned and operated by the defendant town of Barnstable has moved to amend its complaint to add four counts under G.L.c. 214, § 7A, the motion should be allowed because (1) the proposed state-law claims are sufficiently related to the plaintiff’s Clean Water Act claims to form part of the same “case or controversy” for purposes of 28 U.S.C. §1367(a), (2) the plaintiff did not unduly delay in moving to amend,

item.title: Maritime – Counterclaim – Indemnification and contribution
item.description: Where a counterclaim has been asserted in an action under the Limitation of Liability Act, a motion to dismiss should be denied because counterclaims for indemnity and contribution are permissible in a limitation proceeding.

item.title: Employment – Wage Act – Class certification
item.description: Where a plaintiff alleging that the defendant employer violated the Massachusetts Wage Act has moved to certify a “monthly pay class” of the defendant’s employees, the motion should be allowed because individual differences in damages do not preclude class certification.

item.title: Labor – Injunction
item.description: Where a plaintiff union has moved for injunctive relief to prevent a defendant from implementing a planned voluntary separation program pending resolution of the union’s grievance regarding the program, the union “has failed to demonstrate that this is one of the rare cases warranting issuance of a labor injunction,” so the motion should be denied.

item.title: Retirement – Accidental disability – Heart law
item.description: Where a petitioner who suffered a heart attack filed an application to retire for accidental disability, the State Board of Retirement’s denial of the application should be affirmed because the petitioner’s evidence, taken as unrebutted and believed, did not establish that her preemployment physical examination failed to reveal any evidence of a heart condition.

item.title: Administrative – Women Business Enterprise – Certification
item.description: Where the Supplier Diversity Office denied an application for certification as a Women Business Enterprise, the denial should be upheld because the applicant has not shown that it is an ongoing, independent business controlled by one or more women.

item.title: Administrative – Nurse Aide Registry – Misappropriation
item.description: Where a home health aide has admitted to misappropriating property from her client, that information must be listed on the Nurse Aide Registry maintained by the Department of Public Health.

item.title: Habeas corpus – Instructional error – 18 U.S.C. §924(c)
item.description: Where a petitioner moved under 28 U.S.C. §2255 to vacate his two convictions for violating 18 U.S.C. §924(c), a U.S. District Court judge’s decision to deny the motion should be affirmed despite the fact that the jury instructions in the petitioner’s trial were rendered erroneous by United States v. Davis, 588 U.S. 445 (2019).

item.title: Cannabis regulators mull extension to help struggling delivery licensees
item.description: Massachusetts cannabis regulators consider extending the delivery license exclusivity period to help social equity applicants overcome industry challenges.

item.title: Labor secretary’s spouse not charged but remains banned from agency
item.description: Shawn DeRemer, husband of Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer, remains banned from the Department of Labor headquarters amid sexual misconduct allegations despite no criminal charges.
